I found no defensible BF16 defect in the frozen snapshot, and I want to be clear about what that does and does not mean. It means the selector code at commit `83a34c7` does what you approved, as far as reading the code can establish. It does not mean BF16 has been shown running in the integrated application, because that proof still belongs to the root session and I was instructed not to build, run tests, load models, or touch the GPU.

I reviewed the commit through git objects rather than the working tree, so root's separate uncommitted mask fixes could not contaminate the verdict. The tree at `83a34c7` is byte-identical to `d19218c6ab60b838a85049f31872bfef7cac556b`, and its parent is `01697be`, exactly as your brief described. I read the private selector in full at [uct_runtime_precision.hpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/src/common/uct_runtime_precision.hpp:1), the TensorRT network construction, preparation worker, status handling, and both factories in [uct_tensorrt.cpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/src/common/uct_tensorrt.cpp:277), and the candidate wiring in [uct_paddle.cpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/src/common/uct_paddle.cpp:140). I also traced the supporting definitions those paths depend on, including the profile matcher in [uct_recognizer_width.hpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/src/common/uct_recognizer_width.hpp:46), the model pins in [uct_model_pins.hpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/include/okuflow/common/uct_model_pins.hpp), and asset verification and the default model root in [uct_paddle_processing.cpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/src/common/uct_paddle_processing.cpp:47). I read the three new test slots and their registration, the new page at [uct_local_bf16.md](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/docs/uct_local_bf16.md:1), and the accompanying changes to the code reference, hardcoded-paths page, developer guide, Ultra Clear Text page, changelog, and agent guide, along with the third-party license section for the optional PaddleOCR and TensorRT components.

The pinning is genuinely strict, and every mismatch I traced fails closed rather than improvising. The manifest must be schema 1 with an explicit `prepare=false`, it is capped at 64 KiB, and both graph roles must carry exactly the approved precision labels and hashes, as shown in [uct_runtime_precision.hpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/src/common/uct_runtime_precision.hpp:94). The recognizer graph path must be the exact pinned location under the artifact root, and the detector path must match the normal runtime's medium detector, so the manifest cannot quietly redirect detection to some other file. Before the plan is accepted, the code resolves canonical paths to defeat link escapes, rehashes the converted graph, rehashes the whole plan file against `155c74b5…e6f5495`, and checks the existing 32-byte payload digest header, all in [uct_runtime_precision.hpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/src/common/uct_runtime_precision.hpp:138). I verified the real artifacts on disk match those pins: the manifest at `Z:/Projects/OkuFlow/local-work-data/uct-quantization-20261022/manifests/bf16-linear-rec-cached.json` contains the expected hashes and your LocalAppData detector path, the plan file hashes to the pinned whole-file value and is 40,898,276 bytes, and the converted graph hashes to `ecd8ffc9…f94e5835`. The production plan key also genuinely recreates the experiment's key. I compared it against the experiment function at commit `999d058` and the identity strings are equivalent for this fixed profile, including the raw UUID byte handling, and the resulting `e596b8ac…496073` name is the actual plan filename on disk.

The boundary around who may use this is also clean. A search across the frozen tree confirms the environment variable is read in exactly one production place, the private factory at [uct_tensorrt.cpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/src/common/uct_tensorrt.cpp:1256), and that factory is called only for the normal first GPU candidate in [uct_paddle.cpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/src/common/uct_paddle.cpp:153). The public factory constructs the recognizer without a precision request, so diagnostics and injected candidates stay on FP32 and never look at the selector. The three-candidate order and the Windows preparation bridge at index 2 are unchanged, and the supplemental path still cannot promote, retire, or start the bridge, because none of that logic was touched.

The failure classification is the part I pressed hardest, and it holds. Only the typed artifact error permits the preparation worker to fall back to cached FP32, and that error is raised only for manifest, path, hash, FLOAT I/O, and exact-profile rejections, with a stream synchronization guard before the FP32 attempt at [uct_tensorrt.cpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/src/common/uct_tensorrt.cpp:1129). Deserialization failure is deliberately a plain runtime failure, execution-context creation happens after the profile checks and also fails the whole candidate, and genuine inference faults still go through ordinary retirement, so nothing launders a runtime fault into a second BF16-to-FP32 inference attempt. Whenever your selector is nonempty, both networks and the FP32 fallback are cache-only: the builder is never loaded, the baseline cache directory is not created, the batch-cascade retry is disabled, and a missing FP32 cache simply leaves the GPU candidate unavailable for the normal CPU and Windows fallback. With the selector empty, the preparation expressions reduce to the previous baseline behavior.

One point I checked carefully and cleared concerns the TensorRT version. The device record carries `11.4.0.106` as its default rather than querying it at key-construction time, which looks like a tautology in [uct_runtime_precision.hpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/src/common/uct_runtime_precision.hpp:44). In practice the effective gate is real, because the library loader verifies the loaded DLL reports exactly version 11.4.0.106 before any engine is deserialized, at [uct_tensorrt.cpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/src/common/uct_tensorrt.cpp:200). A wrong runtime therefore fails the whole GPU candidate rather than selecting FP32 on the GPU, but that is also the pre-existing baseline position, since the same loader pin governs FP32. I do not consider that a BF16 defect.

The reported status is truthful in the ways you specified. Before validation it says the BF16 request is not yet validated, after success it describes a BF16-linear recognition graph with mixed BF16, FP16, and FP32 arithmetic and FLOAT I/O alongside the FP32 medium detector, and after rejection it names actual FP32 with the fallback reason, through [uct_runtime_precision.hpp](/Z:/Projects/T3-worktrees/oku_flow/t3-adc7d6cc/src/common/uct_runtime_precision.hpp:173). Nothing claims pure BF16, full-mantissa FP32, ground-truth accuracy, or performance on other hardware, and the documentation preserves the original 5 percent and 10-pixel comparison failures as failures that you accepted knowingly.

What remains unvalidated is everything that requires execution, and none of it should be inferred from my reading. I did not rerun the CPU policy gate that your brief reports as passing, and that gate cannot compile the enabled TensorRT branch in any case. Nobody in this review has compiled the CUDA configuration, deserialized the plan through the actual production factory on your RTX 4090, confirmed that the required FP32 detector cache is present for the cache-only path, or seen BF16 engage in the launched application. The combined CPU, CUDA, shared-source, and precompiled-header checks, the environment enablement, and the launch all remain with root, as does any retirement-observer or diagnostic delta root may add, since none of that exists in the snapshot I reviewed. I also did not re-derive the experiment's quality or timing statistics, and I kept the separate regional and mask repair lines, including the Astra r10 items and patch `6a9f301`, entirely outside this verdict, as you instructed.
